ic_name: NFC / ISO 14443 (NXP AN10833 MIFARE family — subset)

registers.name: ATQA
registers.description: 16-bit identification field returned by the PICC.

registers.name: UID
registers.description: Unique PICC serial number; UID byte 0 = Manufacturer Byte.

registers.name: BCC_per_CL
registers.long_name: Block Check Character per Cascade Level
registers.access: Computed by both PCD and PICC
registers.description: 8-bit XOR of the 4 UID bytes within the current Cascade Level.

registers.name: SAK
registers.description: 8-bit classification byte; bit 3 = UID not complete; bit 6 = ISO 14443-4 compliant.

registers.name: GetVersion_Response
registers.description: 7-byte version frame; byte 2 = HW Product Type.

registers.name: ATQB
registers.description: Type B equivalent of ATQA + UID + SAK.

registers.name: PCB
registers.description: First byte of every T=CL Layer-4 block.

registers.name: CID
registers.access: Read/Write (assigned by PCD at RATS PARAM)

base_address: Defined at SoC level; offsets given relative to module base.
notes: ISO/IEC 14443 itself does not standardise a host-bus register map; what it standardises are on-card identification structures (ATQA, UID + SAK per Cascade Level, ATS) and a small set of MIFARE family classification 'pseudo-registers' that AN10833 documents as the deterministic identity surface of every PICC. PCD reader chips (CLRC663, PN512, MFRC522) implement their own host-side register file behind SPI/I2C/UART — those are vendor-specific and out of scope here.
